title: Conditions Without si in Market Forecasts

sections.content:
You know conditions without *si* using *de* + infinitive from B2 Unit 10. In economic commentary and policy forecasts, *de* + infinitive is one of the most common ways to compress a scenario into an opening phrase before stating its likely outcome.

*De* + simple infinitive expresses a possible or hypothetical condition (*De seguir así*, *De no bajar las tasas*, *De mantenerse esta tendencia*) and pairs with the future, present or simple conditional in the main clause. *De* + compound infinitive (*haber* + participle) expresses an unfulfilled past condition (*De haberse frenado antes la inflación*) and pairs with the conditional or compound conditional. A gerund can also state a condition when both clauses share a subject (*Reduciendo el gasto, se evitaría el estancamiento*).

sections.title: Compressed conditional patterns
rows: De seguir así, la inversión caerá. (= Si sigue así...)
De no bajar las tasas, el consumo se frenará. (= Si no bajan...)
De haberse aplicado antes, habría evitado la recesión. (= Si se hubiera aplicado...)
Aumentando la inversión, se impulsaría el crecimiento. (= Si se aumentara...)

items.spanish: De mantenerse esta tendencia, la desaceleración durará varios meses.
items.english: If this trend continues, the slowdown will last several months.

items.spanish: De no cambiar la política monetaria, el estancamiento podría prolongarse.
items.english: If monetary policy does not change, stagnation could drag on.

items.spanish: De haber pedido el préstamo antes, la empresa pagaría menos intereses.
items.english: Had the company taken out the loan earlier, it would be paying less interest.

items.spanish: Frenando el gasto público, el gobierno evitaría una recesión mayor.
items.english: By curbing public spending, the government would avoid a deeper recession.

sections.content: After *de*, always use an infinitive, never a conjugated verb: write *De no bajar las tasas*, never *De no bajan las tasas* or *De no bajaran las tasas*. Place *no* directly between *de* and the infinitive, and attach any reflexive or object pronoun to the infinitive (*de mantenerse*, *de haberlo previsto*). Set the opening phrase off with a comma.
